t:
Service performed during the period January 1, 1984,  through December 31, 1986, which would, if performed after that period, be considered service as a law enforcement officer, as defined in section 8401(17) (A)(i)(II) and (B) of title 5, United States Code, shall be deemed service as a law enforcement officer for the purposes of chapter 84 of such title.
This Act may be cited as the “Treasury, Postal Service, and General Government Appropriations Act, 1996”.

fable.w: The section only deems certain 1984-1986 service to be law enforcement officer service for federal retirement purposes and gives the Act's short title. There is no tempting participation reading here: no outside party is consulted, heard, placed on an advisory body, or given a right to sue, and no rulemaking is authorized.

qwen_block.w: This section defines how certain past service is credited for retirement or benefit purposes under Chapter 84 of Title 5. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. It is purely an administrative definition regarding employee benefits.
qwen_block.s: Service performed during the period January 1, 1984, through December 31, 1986, which would, if performed after that period, be considered service as a law enforcement officer... shall be deemed service as a law enforcement officer for the purposes of chapter 84 of such title.

opus.w: The section says that service from 1984 through 1986 counts as law enforcement officer service under chapter 84 of title 5, and it gives the Act's short title. Neither provision involves anyone outside the federal government in a federal decision. There is no consultation, advisory body, comment period, hearing or right to sue, so nothing in the section is even on-topic for participation.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** There isn't much of one. The phrase "law enforcement officer" might suggest that outsiders take part in government. But the section only says how earlier federal service is treated for retirement purposes, and then gives the Act's short title. No one outside the federal government is consulted, sits on a panel, comments, attends a hearing or gets a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a definitional provision that clarifies which past service counts as 'law enforcement officer' service for federal retirement benefits. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government. The definition relies on existing statutory language and does not create a process for external input.
qwen_chat.s: Service performed during the period January 1, 1984, through December 31, 1986, which would, if performed after that period, be considered service as a law enforcement officer, as defined in section 8401(17) (A)(i)(II) and (B) of title 5, United States Code, shall be deemed service as a law enforcement officer for the purposes of chapter 84 of such title.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that defining "law enforcement officer" involves some external input or consultation, but the text is purely definitional and retroactive, applying existing statutory definitions to a specific time period. There is no mention of consulting with outside parties, holding hearings, or involving non-federal entities in any decision-making process. The text simply clarifies eligibility for federal benefits (retirement under chapter 84) based on service history.
